regulatory.note: FDA guidance, regulations.gov, ONC/ASTP, CMS. High floor, slow decay — a regulatory action stays relevant long after it's announced.

peer_reviewed.note: PubMed/NCBI E-utilities. Same treatment as regulatory — published, reviewed findings don't stale out in days.

preprint.note: arXiv, medRxiv. Low floor, fast decay — unreviewed, and today's preprint is stale news within days unless it's still trending (the rolling-window dedup store's job, not this rubric's).

industry_press.note: STAT News, Fierce Healthcare, Healthcare IT News. Same treatment as preprint — timely but not authoritative on its own; a claim from here should usually be corroborated, not cited standalone.

sources.name: ONC/ASTP
sources.feed_url_verified_note: Confirmed live via the broadcast-live-smoke-test workflow (GitHub Actions run, 2026-09-02): 10 real items, parsed correctly by the existing generic RSS parser (fetch_rss/parse_rss_xml, same one built for STAT News/Fierce Healthcare) with no code changes needed — real dates parsed as standard RFC 822, no pubDate-format fix required unlike fierce_healthcare. Three guessed alternate slugs (/rss.xml on this path, and healthit.gov's site-root /feed which is a much shorter, non-blog feed) were checked and ruled out first.

sources.name: CMS
sources.feed_url_verified_note: Confirmed live via the broadcast-live-smoke-test workflow (GitHub Actions run, 2026-09-02): 10 real items. The URL itself serves RSS XML directly (no separate HTML links page to scrape). Needed two real fixes to the shared RSS parser, not just a feed_url: this feed's <link> field is corrupted (a URL-percent-encoded copy of the <title>'s own markup, not a clean URL — recovered from the title's <a href> instead), and its <pubDate> uses a third undocumented format ('Tue, 09/01/2026 - 09:02') beyond RFC 822 and fierce_healthcare's. Also surfaced a pre-existing description-cleaning bug (multi-paragraph text glued together with no space) fixed in the same pass.

sources.name: STAT News
sources.feed_url_verified_note: Confirmed live via the broadcast-live-smoke-test workflow (GitHub Actions run, 2026-09-01): 20 real items returned once fetch_rss sent a browser-like User-Agent.

sources.name: Fierce Healthcare
sources.feed_url_verified_note: Confirmed live (2026-09-01): 25 real items. The URL was fine on the first try; the real bug was that this feed's <pubDate> isn't RFC 822 ('Sep 1, 2026 2:08pm' — no day-of-week, 12hr+am/pm, no timezone), which silently zeroed every item until _parse_rss_pubdate() got a fallback format for it.

sources.name: Healthcare IT News
sources.feed_url_verified_note: Confirmed BLOCKED, not just unverified (2026-09-01): HTTP 403 on this URL and three other guessed variants (/rss.xml, /feed), even with a full Chrome-like header set (User-Agent, Accept, Accept-Language, Referer). Looks like WAF/Cloudflare-style bot protection a plain HTTP client can't pass — needs a different approach (headless browser, an alternate syndication endpoint, or a manual check for whether they offer one) before this source can actually be ingested. Left broken and documented rather than silently dropped or faked working.
